$comment: The CDP tracking plan (window 16, #554). One entry per event topic we map onto a CDP call, and every topic we do NOT map listed with the reason. Properties are ids, integer minor-unit amounts with their currency, countries, counts and email_hash — never a name, address, phone number or e-mail (ADR 0003 item 5). The mapper in apps/engagement/src/cdp is driven by this file and its tests assert the two agree, so a topic added here without a mapping, or mapped without an entry, fails the suite.

identity.$comment: How a CDP identity is resolved, in this order. `customer_id` is our own id and the only stable key; email_hash is a fallback that cannot be reversed and is never the upsert key for a known customer.

resolution.$comment: The five order-scoped topics carry neither customer_id nor email_hash in their payload, so the identity is read from the `order` row through the same store-scoped tenant client (and in the same query) as the consent projection. One read per event, never a second source of truth.

consent.$comment: Owner decision 2026-10-23 (#576): analytics tracking of our own commerce events does not require a marketing consent, and a guest may be tracked under their email_hash. Region rules are applied as CONFIG, not code, so the mode resolves per store.

mode.analytics: track and identify run without marketing_email; a guest with no customer_id is tracked under email_hash. The only remaining drop is having no identity at all.
mode.strict: what #554 shipped: no identify and no track without granted marketing_email for that store, and a guest is dropped.
mode.note: Each brand is one market (A=EU, B=UK, C=US), so a per-store override is a per-region override. An unknown mode value fails the boot rather than falling back to the open mode.

consent.evaluated: at processing time, never from the event payload
consent.note: customer.created and customer.updated carry a marketing_consent field; the mapper ignores it on purpose, so a decision here can contradict the event own snapshot when consent changed in between. In analytics mode consent is not consulted for a track at all.
consent.erased_customers: An erased customer is never sent, in EITHER mode: the erasure already told every consumer to delete its copies, so tracking that person again would undo it.
consent.always_ungated: customer.erased, which suppresses the identity (customer_id, and email_hash when known)

events.$comment: Ids only, in BOTH consent modes (#576). `status` and `customer_group_id` were here and are deliberately gone: `status` is not an id, and a customer group is a marketing SEGMENT id, which is the kind of trait an identify must not carry. The CDP builds its own audiences from the tracked events.

Ids only, in BOTH consent modes (#576). `status` and `customer_group_id` were here and are deliberately gone: `status` is not an id, and a customer group is a marketing SEGMENT id, which is the kind of trait an identify must not carry. The CDP builds its own audiences from the tracked events.
An erasure is honoured whatever the consent said: it is the one call that must go out for a customer who has withdrawn everything.

events.name: Order Completed
events.$comment: Named for RudderStack's e-commerce spec. Line items are reduced to counts: the per-line titles and SKUs are not needed for a CDP audience and every property we send is one more thing to justify.

events.name: Order Shipped
events.$comment: No tracking_number: it identifies a parcel at a carrier and reaches a third party with nothing gained for an audience.

events.name: Product Returned
events.$comment: No reason: free text a customer or an agent typed, the same rule the ops alerts follow (#553).

unmapped.reason: our own configuration, not customer behaviour
catalogue state; a CDP wants behaviour, and the product catalogue reaches it from the feeds (window 17)
internal lifecycle steps between placed and shipped; they would add CDP events an audience cannot act on. Revisit if a lifecycle audience is ever asked for.
operational, not behavioural — these are the ops-alert topics (#553). A failed payment in a marketing audience would be a dark pattern.
warehouse-side steps. shipment.delivered is the one worth revisiting (a review request audience); it is out until someone asks.
the warehouse side of a return; return.requested is the customer's action and is mapped
a privacy-request lifecycle; sending it to a third party would be the opposite of its purpose

window 17's marketing domain. cart.abandoned and attribution.recorded are the obvious CDP candidates, but they belong to marketing's own flows (Klaviyo, deferred until an account exists) and double-sending them would double-count an audience. A REQUEST to window 17 before any of these is mapped.
